evidence: The reviewer traced that prior.reviews is gated to parseAgentArtifact kind 'review' and projected to {id, state, dismissed}, so `(r.body || '').trimEnd() === body` can never match; the agent confirmed it by reading summarizePriorReviews, and the fix (commit 04dae9e) collected RELEASE_FAILED_MARKER bodies ahead of that gate, with an end-to-end test through the real summarizePriorReviews.
guidance_note: When a dedup reads prior artifacts, write its test through the production fetch-and-project path (summarizePriorReviews), not the fake host's internal store, so the fixture cannot carry fields the real projection drops.

evidence: The flagged commit 2cb8c78 only bumps package-lock's version; the real cause is F1's fix, which made the exact-body dedup (`releaseFailureBodies.includes(body)`) live without making its key stable, while the message joins review ids in listReviews order, which the file itself documents Gitea does not keep stable across calls. The agent sorted `outstanding` by id and added a two-review reverse-order regression test.
guidance_note: When fixing a dedup so it can actually match, also check that the key it compares is deterministic: sort any joined collection that comes from a host listing before rendering it into the compared text.

narrative: The PR added a deduplicated BLOCK NOT RELEASED notice, but the dedup read a projection that had no body field, so it was dead code; the test passed only because it read the fake host's store. The fix (landed by a concurrent session) made the dedup live, and the next round found that its exact-text key depended on unstable listReviews ordering. Both findings were real, and both were accepted and fixed with mutation-checked tests.
guidance_observations: Two sessions worked the same finding at once and the agent had to discover and verify the other one's commit; one owner per PR thread would have saved that time.
Both defects were in the same exact-text dedup: the first fix should have asked whether the key could ever match, and also whether it would match on the next fetch.

evidence: `case 'bot': return user?.type === 'Bot'` admits any installed app, and the comment said it needed 'control of a GitHub App installed on this repo', so the comment overclaimed. The agent took the reviewer's second option (document the real guarantee) and gave a checkable reason for declining the pin: an installation token cannot name its own app, and hardcoding github-actions[bot] would reject create-github-app-token consumers' own rounds.
guidance_note: When writing a structural predicate's comment, state the full set of accounts it admits (here, every installed Bot), not the attacker bar you hope it imposes.

evidence: The reviewer quoted CLAUDE.md's rubric, which ties minor to the input surface, and action.yml was untouched; the agent agreed the written rule governs and dropped the version to 1.49.2.
guidance_note: Before bumping package.json, check the change against the repo's written semver rubric (did action.yml's inputs or defaults change?) instead of judging how big the change feels.

evidence: With a single resolved identity, setting GITHUB_REVIEW_TOKEN mid-PR (which the README recommends) disowns earlier bot-posted rounds and drops an outstanding REQUEST_CHANGES out of the set releaseUnrevisitableBlocks can dismiss. The agent changed the identity to a set of distinct tokens; that fix then produced F9, F11, F12, F14, F15 and F18.
guidance_note: Before shipping an identity gate over history a PR already has, list every configuration transition the docs recommend (adding, rotating, or unsetting GITHUB_REVIEW_TOKEN) and check which past authors each one strands.

evidence: Only the 403 arm of resolveReviewerIdentity was covered, and only indirectly through run(); the 200/login path, the no-login throw and the non-403 throw had no tests. The agent added a direct suite covering every arm, including the reworked installation confirmation.
guidance_note: Give a new security gate one direct unit test per arm, including each throw, in the same commit that adds it.

evidence: `if (e.status === 403) return { kind: 'bot' }` inferred an installation token from any 403, so a PAT refused on /user would be misclassified and its own type-User reviews disowned. Instead of measuring fine-grained PATs, the agent positively confirmed the installation with GET /installation/repositories, which makes the fine-grained-PAT question moot; the agent's own reply says the measurement was 'already in hand'.
guidance_note: When a measurement gives a positive signal for a token kind (here, /installation/repositories answering 200), branch on that signal, never on an error status from a different endpoint.

evidence: Same defect as F5: secondary rate limits and SSO also return 403. The reviewer suggested matching the error message; the agent used the installation-probe confirmation instead, which drops the reliance on GitHub's error wording and still reaches the loud throw the reviewer asked for.
guidance_note: When a function's doc block promises 'anything else throws', check that every early return in the code is an established fact, not a guess from an error status.

evidence: This is the third thread on the same line. The reviewer correctly said the any-403 return contradicted the doc block's 'Anything else is an UNRESOLVED identity and throws'; the agent applied the same confirmation-probe fix, not the message match the reviewer suggested.
guidance_note: Before pushing, compare each early return against the function's stated contract; this one contradicted its own doc block.

evidence: The comment beside forkNotice still called the round-cap marker forgery an accepted risk awaiting zai-review-trust-6yp, the ticket this PR closes, even though CLAUDE.md and README had been updated. The agent rewrote it and recorded why the fork path's latestArtifact null stays independent of the author gate.
guidance_note: When a PR closes a ticket, grep the whole tree for that ticket id and for the risk wording it tracked, and update every hit, in-code comments included.

evidence: F3's fix added distinctTokens threading in run.js, but pr-review-gate.test.js's `github.getOctokit = () => fakeOctokit()` threw away the token, so nothing proved run.js passed both credentials. The agent made the fake depend on its token and added two tests; one of them later turned out vacuous (F17).
guidance_note: When a fix adds glue between entry point and unit (distinctTokens into resolveReviewerIdentities), make the integration fake depend on its inputs and mutation-check the new test before pushing.

evidence: The comment 'The forgery cases below supply an author' pointed at tests that live in skip-notice.test.js, not in this file; the agent corrected the pointer. The packet does not show whether this comment predates the round-0 fix commit, so no cause is assigned.
guidance_note: When a test comment refers to 'cases below', check that they really are in this file before committing.

evidence: F3's fix turned identity into an array and put the empty-set refusal inside isOwnArtifact, which only runs inside the per-review loop, so a PR with zero reviews returned count 0 without refusing. Commit 7dc9817 shows requireIdentities moved ahead of the pagination loop.
guidance_note: When adding a precondition check, put it where it runs on every call, not inside a loop that can run zero times, and test the zero-iteration input.

evidence: F3's fix wrote `[...new Set([reviewToken || token, token])]` beside the existing `getOctokit(reviewToken || token)`, two copies of the posting-token rule. Commit 7dc9817 introduces `const postingToken` and both call sites read it.
guidance_note: When a fix needs a value an earlier line already computes inline, extract it to a named const and reuse it; don't retype the expression.

evidence: F9's fix added run.js glue tests for the success path only; the catch path (`core.setFailed(e.message); return;`) on an identity throw stayed untested. Commit 6e2c3f2 adds brokenIdentityTokens and asserts no engine spawn, no post, and one failure.
guidance_note: When adding integration coverage for new glue, write the failure-arm test with the success-arm test (here, both probes refuse, so the run must red without spending).

evidence: F3's fix documented the set as 'every token the run holds', but run.js resolves only [postingToken, token] and leaves out DISMISS_TOKEN. The reply-hint says pushback, but the agent agreed and narrowed both docs in 6e2c3f2 (the diff shows 'every token that can *post a review*').
guidance_note: When describing a set in docs, copy the literal membership from the code ([postingToken, token]) instead of writing a general phrase like 'every token the run holds'.

evidence: F3's fix wrote 'Duplicates are collapsed so the common single-token run resolves once', but the loop awaits resolveReviewerIdentity for every octokit before sameIdentity runs, so only run.js's token-string Set saves a probe. The 6e2c3f2 diff rewords the comment to say exactly that.
guidance_note: When a comment claims a cost saving, trace which line actually skips the call; here the saving comes from the caller's token-string dedup, not this function.

evidence: The claim 'Gitea serves /user for its own token' was unmeasured; the same comment is already in round-0 hunks, so the ON-POST-REVIEW flag is a false positive for unchanged text. The later live measurement showed GET /user answers 200 with login gitea-actions, so the feared every-run regression does not happen; the agent declined the fixture test, held the thread open, and verified on a real Gitea, which was the right call.
guidance_note: When a hard-failing gate rests on one host's behavior, measure it on that host before the PR opens, as was done for GitHub, or mark it unmeasured in every doc at once.

evidence: F9's fix added 'builds a client from each distinct credential', but octokitTokens already held both tokens from the reading and posting clients at the top of runPrReview, so the test passed with the identity wiring deleted. The agent admitted it ('this was my test from the previous round') and deleted it in 6e2c3f2.
guidance_note: Mutation-check every new test against the line it claims to guard before pushing; this one passes with the identity call removed.

evidence: F3's fix documented rotation as 'the one transition this cannot cover', but unsetting GITHUB_REVIEW_TOKEN also collapses distinctTokens to [token] and disowns the PAT-authored rounds. The 0fc2aa2 diff restates the limit as a class (a credential the run no longer holds) in both README and CLAUDE.md.
guidance_note: When documenting what a fix does not cover, derive the residual from the predicate (which authors can fall outside distinctTokens) instead of naming one example and calling it the only one.

evidence: The F16 response (6e2c3f2) added 'REASONED FROM SHAPE AND NOT YET MEASURED' to transport.js but left CLAUDE.md asserting 'Gitea serves /user' as fact; the agent admitted 'one clock fixed, the other still running'. The reviewer also asked for a README pointer, which the agent did not add, and that became F22.
guidance_note: When revising a claim's certainty, grep for every place the claim is stated (code comment, CLAUDE.md, README) and change them in one commit.

evidence: F1's fix stated the bot arm's coarseness in the code comment and CLAUDE.md, but the README kept 'ignores any review written by anyone else', which reads as exact attribution. The 0fc2aa2 README diff adds the PAT-versus-default-token paragraph.
guidance_note: When a finding says a guarantee is overstated, fix every doc that states it, including the operator-facing README, not only the comment the reviewer pointed at.

evidence: This re-raises F16, which the agent had deliberately left open; the ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag on 0fc2aa2 is a false positive, because that commit only edited docs and the unmeasured Gitea assumption predates review. The reviewer asked to verify on a live Gitea before merge, and the agent did: GET /user returned 200 with login gitea-actions on 2026-08-26, before the 13:44 merge, so the feared regression was disproven.

F19 explicitly asked to 'add at least a pointer to it in README.md', but the F19 fix commit 0fc2aa2 changed only CLAUDE.md's Gitea text, so the README still had no Gitea risk. The agent added it in 312989a.
guidance_note: When a finding lists several requested edits, check each one off against the diff before replying 'Fixed'.

narrative: The PR added an author-identity gate over prior-review markers, and round 0 found real defects: three threads on the same any-403 bug, an identity-change deadlock, missing tests, and a stale comment. The F3 fix (identity as a set) caused six later findings: a misplaced empty-set guard, a duplicated token expression, missing and vacuous glue tests, and three docs that overstated or under-listed the set. Every certainty or coarseness change landed in some docs and not others (F1 to F20, F16 to F19 to F22), which kept the PR going until it hit the round cap. The one open question, Gitea's /user behavior, was settled by a live measurement before merge.
guidance_observations: Most later findings were the same fact restated in three places (code comment, CLAUDE.md, README), each fix updating only some; one grep per claim per fix would have removed most of rounds 3 and 4.
The agent mutation-checked tests in later rounds but not the round-1 glue test, which shipped vacuous; mutation-checking every new test from the first fix would have caught F17.
Keeping F16 open until a live Gitea measurement, instead of adding a fixture that encodes the assumption, was the right handling of an unverifiable claim and avoided a fake-coverage test.

evidence: `dismissOctokit = dismissToken ? github.getOctokit(dismissToken) : undefined` has no host check, so 'ignored on GitHub' was false. The agent took the reviewer's docs option over a host gate, which would have forced resolving the lazy transport thunk just to pick a credential, and also renamed GITEA_DISMISS_TOKEN to DISMISS_TOKEN because the name itself asserted the gate.
guidance_note: When naming and documenting a new input, describe what the code does with it (used whenever set), not the deployment it is meant for; a host word in the name asserts a branch the code doesn't have.

evidence: This duplicates F1 at the README row: 'ignored on GitHub' had no matching code branch. It was fixed by the same rename and doc rewrite in edc6702, and check-readme-inputs.js would have caught a half-done rename.
guidance_note: Before stating 'ignored on X' in any doc, point to the code branch that skips it; if there is none, don't write the sentence.

narrative: The PR added a Gitea-oriented dismissal credential whose docs and name said it was ignored on GitHub, while the code used it on any host. The reviewer raised this twice (code site and README row). The agent kept the host-agnostic dataflow, renamed the unreleased input to DISMISS_TOKEN, and corrected every doc; round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: Renaming an unreleased input to remove a false claim at its source was cheaper and more durable than adding caveats at four documentation sites.
